questions.question: Development aid is defined as:
options: The transfer of money, goods, technology or expertise from richer countries and institutions to poorer ones, on terms softer than the market's
Remittances sent home by migrant workers

questions.question: Aid pooled through the World Bank, UN agencies or the African Development Bank is called:
Development co-operation differs from traditional aid language because:
options: It involves larger amounts of money
It frames a partnership with obligations on both sides — recipients set priorities and account for results, donors align with the recipient's own plans

questions.question: South Africa 'sits on both sides of the table' because it:
options: Receives aid — notably health funding — while extending assistance within Africa through the African Renaissance Fund and trilateral projects

subtopics.title: Types of Aid: Technical, Conditional and Humanitarian

questions.question: Technical aid's characteristic strength is that:
options: A skill keeps working after the money is spent once — engineers, agronomists and trainers leave permanent capacity behind
It arrives faster than any other type

questions.question: Procurement tying means:
options: Aid must be repaid with interest
The recipient must spend the aid on the donor's own goods and firms, recycling much of the money back to the donor and inflating costs
The recipient chooses any supplier by tender

questions.question: The structural adjustment programmes of the 1980s and 1990s are cited as the hard case of:
options: Policy conditionality — loans requiring spending cuts, privatisation and open markets, which in many African countries gutted health and education budgets

questions.question: Judging emergency food aid for failing to industrialise a country is called a category error because:
options: Food aid always industrialises countries eventually
Short-term relief stops the bleeding while long-term development aid builds the hospital — they answer different problems

subtopics.title: When Aid Works: The Positive Case

questions.question: Aid's single most complete triumph is:
options: The eradication of smallpox through an aid-funded global vaccination campaign

questions.question: PEPFAR and Global Fund financing mattered to South Africa because:
options: They funded the national road network
They helped carry the world's largest antiretroviral programme, and life expectancy climbed back from the low fifties to above sixty
They replaced the national health budget entirely
They funded only research, never treatment

questions.question: Aid 'catalysing' investment means:
options: A grant that de-risks a port or power plant can unlock private investment many times its size

questions.question: The honest generalisation across aid's successes is that aid works best when:
options: It is as large as possible
It is spread across many small unrelated projects
It targets specific, measurable problems, aligns with the recipient's own priorities, and is sustained long enough to finish the job

subtopics.title: When Aid Fails: Dependency, Distortion and Debt

questions.question: Aid dependency develops when:
options: Aid finances a large share of a government's budget year after year, tilting accountability toward donors and weakening the drive to build a tax base
A country repays its loans early

questions.question: Food aid outside genuine emergencies can distort development by:
options: Undercutting local farmers until they stop planting — solving this year's hunger by creating next year's

questions.question: The 1980s-90s debt crisis showed aid 'flowing backwards' because:
options: Many African countries paid more in debt service than they spent on health and education combined

questions.question: The scaffolding verdict on aid holds that:
options: Aid should be permanent for all countries
Aid never helps under any conditions
Scaffolding is more important than the building
Aid is essential during construction but must be designed to come down as the building stands — a tool, not a permanent economic strategy

subtopics.title: Fish, Fishing Lessons and the Flood

questions.question: In the proverb picture, the 'fish' is:
options: Humanitarian aid — the food parcel, rescue boat and blankets, judged by speed and reach

questions.question: 'During the flood, a lesson is useless and a boat is everything' teaches that:
options: Timing decides which aid is right — emergencies need relief, and development needs skills
Boats are a form of technical aid

questions.question: The beached boats — local fishermen unable to compete with free fish — represent:
options: Dependency and market distortion — permanent free aid pushing local producers out until the town waits on the truck

questions.question: The neighbour insisting you buy roof sheets from his shop at his prices stands for:
options: Procurement tying — aid money cycling back to donor companies while costs inflate

questions.question: The neighbour demanding a say in your household budget stands for:
options: Policy conditionality — money flowing only if prescribed policies are adopted, as in the structural adjustment era

questions.question: Naming donors' mixed motives — influence, trade, security alongside solidarity — is described as:
options: An insult to be avoided in essays
Analysis, not insult — the analytical edge the essay question rewards
Proof that all aid is harmful

questions.question: The 'co-operation upgrade' to the gift-with-strings works by:
options: Removing all conditions from every grant
Letting the donor design the renovation alone
The household setting its own plan, the neighbour contributing to that plan, and both signing accountability agreements — obligations both ways

questions.question: Items that belong on the triumphs pan of the scale include:
options: Smallpox eradication, South Africa's ARV programme, steep falls in malaria deaths, and rapid flood relief

questions.question: Items that belong on the failures pan include:
options: Food dumping beaching local farmers, debt eating health budgets, tied money returning to donors, and dependency on donor funding

questions.question: 'Nobody calls scaffolding a house' argues that:
options: Aid supports construction but is not itself development, and if it stays up forever something has gone wrong with the building
Construction is the only true aid

questions.question: The exam-winning conclusion on aid is that it:
options: Works when it targets a specific, finishable job, follows the recipient's own plan, and is designed from day one to become unnecessary
